title: New Orleans drummers and fellow musicians: Dodds, Cantrell, Mac Murray, Foster, Rocells
summary: Baby Dodds as best timekeeper, other drummers, working with Pop and Willie Foster, the Rocells band and Joe Johnson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Until he died just last December. Yeah, last December they say. And he was very good. He was good. And drummers, coming back to drums. Who was one of the best drummers in the last year? I think Baby Dots is one of the best drummers I ever played with. He gave me more time, a better time, twofold, than any drummer that I played with. See, I played with several drummers. Toby Hall is good too, see. And a minor. But Baby Dots is heavy and strong. Regular, you know. If you lose time on anything that you play in it, it's not his fault because he gives you very strict time. And he's very good. Do you remember any old time drummers like Louis Cantrell? Yeah, Louis Cantrell. He was very good. He used to play with an orchestra, one of the best orchestras around New Orleans. He was very, very good. Who's orchestra? He used to play with Robichaud, Robichaud's orchestra. They were very good. They got many dances for mostly. There was parties and there was 400 bunches. They played mostly for them. Did you ever play with Mac Murray? Mac Murray? I played with Mac Murray once or twice.
Maybe you can tell me this. Nobody ever seems to know how it spells name. Was his first name Mac and his last name Murray?

Yeah, I couldn't say M-A-C. M-A-C. M-U-R-R-Y. Is it all one name? What was his first name? They called him Mac, see. Mac was maybe his first name. But his name altogether. I think it was Mac Murray, see. That was his name, Mac Murray. All together, see. Yeah. His first name. His first name. I don't just remember what, but they'd call him Mac, anyway. Mac. Mac. Okay. Yeah. He was, hey, pardon. Did you play with Henry Zeno once or twice? Yeah. I played with him. Pop Foster. And he had a brother, Willie Foster, played the violin. We started an orchestra together. We, Pop Foster, Willie Foster, and a couple of other guys, new guys. And I didn't know they lived in the other part of town, you know, a French part of town. But we all got together and we had a very nice orchestra.
Pop said there was something called the Rocell Band or something. Do you remember that name? Rocells? I don't know. I didn't get the name right.
Yeah. Rocells had a good band. Rocells? Yeah. Rocells. Yeah. Rocells. They had a very good band. Was that the name of the musician? Rocells. Yeah. That was the name of the musician.
And Pop Foster said something about Joe Johnson, the trumpet player.

Yeah. He died. I didn't know much about that. Yeah. You wouldn't give him a new name because he died rather young. Joe Johnson. But he was hot. He was good. He was one who brought this trumpet playing like these fellas play now, see? And he picked that up from Joe Oliver. He lied under those fellas. And he followed their system. Kept up with their system. And he played trumpet just like those fellas. Well, what part of town did you come from? Up town? Up town. Up town.
